guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our numbers are slightly more forgiving of Kennesaw State than the market, and we can see a path to a competitive game through its rushing attack. Kennesaw State ran for 197 yards against Arkansas State, with Boogie Woods III reaching 101 yards and Rickie Collins adding 52. We also note that its defense allowed opponents to convert only 31.9 percent of their third downs through four games, which could help prevent Liberty from completely controlling the game.

We are not treating that improved rushing performance as proof of a breakthrough. Liberty averaged 208.2 rushing yards through five games and called runs on 57.1 percent of its plays, while our efficiency profile also points to an advantage through the air. Liberty had not thrown an interception through five games, so we do not want to assume Kennesaw State can lean on takeaways to offset those offensive advantages.

For us, that creates a modest disagreement rather than a strong position. Kennesaw State has enough mobility and rushing production to stay within range, but Liberty has multiple credible ways to create separation. The available price does not give us enough room to overlook that balance, so we remain on the pass.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Kennesaw State's ability to create scoring opportunities against Liberty's defense. Kennesaw State converted 92.3 percent of its red-zone trips through four games, but it also scored fewer than 20 points in each of the three games following its opener. Liberty entered its next game having held three straight opponents below 20 points and had allowed only a 28.3 percent third-down conversion rate. The question for us is less about whether Kennesaw State can finish drives and more about whether it can generate enough of them.

recent_game.fact: Kennesaw State lost 17-14 at Arkansas State on Sept. 26, 2026, falling to 1-3.
Kennesaw State rushed 38 times for 197 yards and two touchdowns against Arkansas State after averaging 87.0 rushing yards in its previous two games.
Boogie Woods III recorded career highs of 101 rushing yards and two touchdowns against Arkansas State and finished with 121 yards from scrimmage, including 20 receiving yards.
Rickie Collins completed 17 of 24 passes for 129 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed nine times for 52 yards against Arkansas State.
Kennesaw State's offensive line allowed four quarterback hurries and four pressures against Arkansas State.
Linebacker Baron Hopson returned from injury against Arkansas State and recorded eight tackles and 1.5 tackles for loss.

quarterback.fact: Syracuse transfer Rickie Collins won Kennesaw State's quarterback competition and started the 2026 opener.
Through four games, Collins completed 79 of 116 passes for 749 yards, two touchdowns and one interception while rushing 40 times for 185 yards and three touchdowns.
Collins completed at least 60 percent of his passes with at least 20 attempts in each of Kennesaw State's first four games.
Collins had a 68.1 percent completion rate through four games and completed 85.7 percent of his first-quarter passes.
Collins had faced 52 pressures and taken six sacks through four games.

Backup Landon Varnes transferred from Mississippi Gulf Coast after leading the NJCAA in 2025 with 3,296 passing yards, 31 touchdowns and a 177.6 passing-efficiency rating while throwing four interceptions.

offensive_personnel.fact: Kennesaw State returned two offensive starters and lost nine from its 2025 team.
The rebuilt running back group features West Georgia transfer Latrelle Murrell, Benedict College transfer Triston Morgan and Mississippi Gulf Coast transfer Boogie Woods III.
Through four games, Woods had 39 carries for 169 yards and three touchdowns.
Kennesaw State was the only Conference USA team with four players who had each rushed for at least 100 yards and a touchdown through the opening four games.
Northern Colorado transfer Brayden Munroe had 12 receptions for 140 yards through four games, including five catches for 34 yards against Arkansas State.
Javon Rogers had seven receptions for 149 yards through three games, an average of 21.29 yards per reception.
Jamari Harrold made his first career start at tight end against Tennessee and had five receptions for 40 yards and one touchdown through four games.
Reed Jesiolowski had three receptions for 15 yards while taking on a larger role during Gerard Bullock Jr.'s absence.
Kennesaw State returned both 2025 starting offensive tackles, Nikola Milovac and JaDarious Lee, who each started all 14 games in 2025.
The offensive line entered 2026 with more than 240 combined career games and 145 starts, though only 91 games and 58 starts came at Kennesaw State.
JaDarious Lee, Mateo Guevara, Precious Ekeh and Nikola Milovac started each of the first four games on the offensive line; Mike Wallace Jr. started three and Darius Neals started one.

defensive_personnel.fact: Kennesaw State returned five defensive starters and lost seven from its 2025 team.
Transfer edge defender Kai Russell had 17 tackles, two tackles for loss, one sack, three passes defended and one forced fumble through four games.
Baron Hopson had 20 tackles and 1.5 tackles for loss in three appearances through the Arkansas State game.
Tywon Christopher led Kennesaw State with 22 tackles through four games.
Tulsa and North Alabama transfer Josh Anglin had 21 tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss and one sack through four games.
Memphis transfer safety Cam Miller had 21 tackles and one interception through four games after making his first NCAA start against Tennessee.
Miami (Ohio) transfer Luke Evans made his first Kennesaw State start against Tennessee and followed with a career-high nine tackles and one tackle for loss against Arkansas State.
Maryland and UAB transfer Perry Fisher recorded eight tackles in his first Kennesaw State start against Tennessee and seven tackles against Arkansas State.
Defensive linemen Marcus Patterson, Jaiden Grimes and Jackson Cooper started each of the first four games.

coaching_changes.fact: Jerry Mack was in his second season as Kennesaw State's head coach in 2026 after being hired Dec. 1, 2024.
Marc Mattioli remained Kennesaw State's defensive coordinator and safeties coach for a second season in 2026.
Mitch Militello served as offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.

injury_availability.fact: Wide receiver Zion Booker suffered an injury against Arkansas State on Sept. 26 and was announced out for the remainder of the 2026 season.
Tight end Gerard Bullock Jr. missed the Tennessee and Arkansas State games with an injury.
Linebacker Baron Hopson missed the Tennessee game with an injury but returned against Arkansas State on Sept. 26.
Defensive back Tyler Hallum returned against West Georgia after missing the entire 2025 season with an injury; it was his first game in 642 days.

offensive_context.fact: Kennesaw State used a spread base offense and averaged 21.8 points, 167.0 rushing yards, 201.0 passing yards and 368.0 total yards per game through four games.

The offense ranked first in Conference USA in red-zone conversion rate at 92.3 percent and second in sacks allowed, completion percentage, fewest turnovers lost and rushing offense through four games.
Kennesaw State scored fewer than 20 points in each of its three games following the 47-0 opener.
Kennesaw State averaged 21.3 first downs per game through four games.
The Owls averaged 4.9 yards per rushing attempt through four games, up from 4.1 in 2025 and 3.0 in 2024.
Kennesaw State allowed four sacks through four games, an average of one per game.

defensive_context.fact: Kennesaw State used a 4-2-5 base defense and allowed 22.5 points, 166.5 rushing yards, 196.5 passing yards and 363.0 total yards per game through four games.
Excluding the 42 points allowed to Tennessee, Kennesaw State allowed 16.0 points per game in its other three contests.
Kennesaw State forced six fumbles and recovered four through four games.
The defense generated five takeaways through four games: four fumble recoveries and one interception.
Opponents converted 15 of 47 third downs against Kennesaw State through four games, a 31.9 percent rate.
Kennesaw State's defense was on the field for 55.28 percent of total possession time through four games.

special_teams.fact: Running back Triston Morgan returned a kickoff 47 yards and blocked a punt against West Georgia, earning Conference USA Special Teams Player of the Week.

other_relevant.fact: Kennesaw State was 1-3 overall and had not yet played a Conference USA game entering its Oct. 7 game against Jax State.
Kennesaw State returned 49 percent of its overall 2025 production, including 42 percent on offense and 55 percent on defense.
